ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.08 (voucher) for the single unexempt 15:21-15:30 segment; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride Woodlands Civic Centre → Kallang Wave Mall, charged $58.59 on a distance fare of $41.06 for 29.12 km, i.e. a per-km rate of $41.06 ÷ 29.12 km = $1.4100/km [F7][F4][RD-2]. One off-route segment exists: 15:21–15:30, 6.32 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.71 km, adding 3.60 km and straying up to 1425 m from the corridor [F3][RD-1].

Excuses fail. RD-4(a) is unavailable — F15 records no traffic incident near the route in the trip window, and RD-4(b) says a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment, so F12 (PIE band 2, 10–19 km/h, ending 15:21, exactly when F3 begins) is corroboration only [F15][F12][F3][RD-4]. RD-3(a) is unavailable — the rider named no place before the segment and no stop is measured in F3 [F9][F3][RD-3].

RD-5 is the live question. The rider's only pre-segment message is F9 at 15:18, 'Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late.' [F9]. Read in its words it is a general route authorisation: it names no road and no area, so RD-5's named-road branch and G13's correspondence problem are not reached, as D1/D2 rightly argue. But RD-5 gives that general authorisation the reach only of a route chosen to get to the destination; it does not cover a loop of the driver's own. This segment ran 6.32 km where 2.71 km of optimal route existed, 1425 m off any route, and the driver's own account is 'so I went round' [F3][F11]. No rider message asked for that loop. The segment counts, and its 3.60 extra km are refundable under RD-2.

Amount: 3.60 km × $1.4100/km = $5.076 → $5.08 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The billed excess-distance line of $5.88 (4.17 km × $1.4100/km) is larger, but the remaining 0.57 km is corridor/jitter outside any measured segment and is expressly not refundable [F4][F3][RD-2]. The $0.11 waiting charge is a RydeTAXI meter waiting unit and is not part of the claim [F5][RD-3(c)]. RD-6 does not fire: F18 shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so no flag_account [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read every chat message, the driver statement and the complaint [F8][F9][F10][F11] — the exchange is a traffic/routing discussion with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and F15 records no incident. Safety_concern = none.

Evidence: the record settles every element the ruling needs — a measured segment [F3], a complete timestamped chat [F10], and all fare components [F4][F5][F7] — so evidence_status = sufficient, evidence_gap = null, and no escalation ground exists.

segment_findings.reason: The only rider message before the segment's 15:21 start is F9 at 15:18, 'Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late.' [F9][F3]. That is a GENERAL route choice: under RD-5 it covers a route chosen to reach the destination, not a loop of the driver's own. The driven stretch is 6.32 km where the optimal route covers 2.71 km, adding 3.60 km and swinging up to 1425 m off every route [F3], and the driver's own words are 'so I went round' [F11] — nothing the rider asked for and nothing that reaches any stop she named. The rider named no place, so RD-3(a) is unavailable [F9], and no record places the car on any named road. RD-4 gives no excuse: F15 records no incident and a band alone cannot exempt (RD-4(b)) [F15][F12]. The segment is therefore unexempt and refundable under RD-1/RD-2; the driver's post-trip claim of verbal agreement in F11 is not consent (G11).

rejected_claims.reason: F9's 'whichever way is faster' is a general route authorisation that, under RD-5(1), covers a route chosen to get to the destination and not an excursion of the driver's own; the 15:21-15:30 segment ran 6.32 km where the optimal route covers 2.71 km and swung up to 1425 m off every route [F3], so it is a driver-chosen loop no rider message asked for [F8][F9] — the general authorisation does not reach it.

The only corroborating record is a speed band, and RD-4(b) states that a band alone does not exempt a segment; F15 records no traffic incident near the route and F12's band-2 window ends at 15:21, when F3's segment begins.
The $5.88 excess-distance line [F4] traces to the unexempt segment, so the disputed magnitude is not merely nominal; on a metered RydeTAXI trip the extra kilometres enter the fare [F7][F4].

Accepted in its arithmetic but not in its conclusion: the $5.08 cap is right on the amount, yet RD-2/RD-5 require that sum to be refunded rather than nothing; the $0.11 meter waiting charge is correctly excluded [F5][RD-3(c)].
Accepted: RD-6 requires an upheld prior dispute and F18 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so no flag_account is attached.
The aggregate 29.1 km / 46.8 min figures [F1][F2] do not by themselves decide the segment; RD-1 reviews each gps-detour fact individually and here the single segment F3 carries the ruling.

Read as a named-road consent it would make the segment undetermined under RD-5(2)/G13, but the rider's F9 is a general route choice, so the named-road branch is not the applicable reading and no undetermined finding arises.
Accepted: F15 records no incident and F12's band alone cannot exempt under RD-4(b); this supports the refund rather than contradicting the ruling.
Accepted in part: the remaining 0.57 km of billed excess is corridor/jitter and is not refundable under RD-2, which is why the amount is $5.08 and not $5.88.
Accepted: F18 shows 0 upheld disputes so no account flag; the profile facts do not decide the segment either way under RD-6.
